content.title: What Does a Mortgage Broker Do? (With Skills and Salary)
content.text: Career pathsWhat Does a Mortgage Broker Do? (With Skills and Salary)Written byUpdated December 11, 2025What does a mortgage broker do?Loan officers vs. mortgage brokersMortgage broker requirementsMortgage broker work environmentMortgage brokers are an important part of finding commercial and residential real estate for purchasers. They often help their clients find the best mortgage loans for their needs. Understanding the important role this profession has can help you decide if this is the job for you and whether you need a mortgage broker for your next real estate purchase.In this article, we explore what a mortgage broker does, provide a comparison between a mortgage broker and a loan officer, explain the requirements to become a mortgage broker and the process of becoming one.Key takeaways:A mortgage broker acts as an intermediary between a financial institution or lender and a prospective homeowner, helping to secure the best mortgage loan options and complete the application process.To become a successful mortgage broker, one needs a combination of education, licensure and specialized job skills, with an emphasis on customer service, critical thinking, communication and negotiation.Mortgage brokers operate in a fast-paced work environment requiring constant communication, and often work irregular hours to meet the needs of their clients. What does a mortgage broker do?A mortgage broker acts as an intermediary between a financial institution or lender and a prospective homeowner. A residential mortgage broker evaluates the buyer's financial and employment information and gathers mortgage loan options from multiple lenders. Once the buyer selects an option, the broker helps them complete the loan paperwork. A commercial real estate mortgage broker performs the same function for buyers of commercial properties.The daily responsibilities of a mortgage broker include:Establishing professional relationships with mortgage lendersGathering documents, credit history and employment verification of prospective homebuyersProviding the borrower with lending options that best suit their financial situationApplying for mortgage loans on behalf of the borrowerAdvising clients on their options and clearly explaining the legal and repayment details of any available loanEnsuring loans are compliant with all regulations and lawsCompleting all closing paperwork with the lender, title company, insurance broker and any other relevant agencyRead more: Learn About Being a Mortgage BrokerLoan officers vs. mortgage brokersLoan officers are similar to mortgage brokers, though the breadth of materials they work with is larger. Loan officers evaluate, recommend and approve applications for many different types of loans. They often work on behalf of lenders to ensure all applicants meet the requirements for loans and are able to pay the loan back over a period of time. In contrast, mortgage brokers typically work on behalf of mortgage loan recipients, ensuring they get the best loans for their current financial standing.These two professions often interact as mortgage brokers may create applications for loans that loan officers review and approve or deny based on the requirements of their employer.Related: Mortgage Broker vs. Real Estate Broker: What Are Their Roles?Mortgage broker requirementsSuccess as a mortgage broker usually requires a combination of education, licensure and specialized job skills. Below are the primary requirements for becoming a mortgage broker:EducationAt a minimum, mortgage brokers need a high school diploma or a GED to find employment in many organizations. Earning an associate or bachelor's degree in business administration, finance or accounting can expand their job opportunities and possibly increase their earning potential. To maintain an active broker's license, which is a requirement to practice in the U.S., brokers complete continuing education courses to remain current with industry trends and regulations. The number of professional development hours a broker needs to complete depends on the state that issues the license.Related: Mortgage Broker vs. Lender: What Are the Differences?TrainingProspective mortgage brokers also complete a 20-hour training course before taking the licensure exam. The course focuses on topics such as federal and state mortgage laws, broker ethics and mortgage origination. Once a mortgage broker gains employment, they typically continue to learn important skills while working at their job. Their employer teaches them about company-specific practices and provides real-world experiences for them to use throughout their careers. They also learn about specific scheduling software or computer programs the company may use.Related: Mortgage Broker vs. Real Estate Agent: How They DifferCertificationsIn the U.S., the 2008 Secure and Fair Enforcement for Mortgage Licensing Act (SAFE) requires all mortgage brokers to earn licensure by passing both the national and state versions of the SAFE Mortgage Loan Originator Test. The National Mortgage Licensure System (NMLS) administers the test and keeps a record of all current licenses. Mortgage brokers renew their licenses annually to remain compliant with all regulations.Related: 10 Jobs in the Mortgage Industry (Plus Tips for Starting a Career)SkillsMortgage brokers spend a lot of their time establishing and maintaining relationships with lenders and borrowers. They also help people navigate the complicated legal and financial terminology in mortgage documents. For those reasons, it's important to possess some of the following skills and qualities, including:Customer serviceTo generate business and develop good relationships with borrowers and financial institutions, it's vital to have excellent customer service skills. These include being a good listener, responding quickly to phone calls and emails and being able to explain the fine points and details of the application process and closing documents. Brokers employ customer service skills with borrowers to make them feel more comfortable during each step of the process.Related: How To Start Your Career in the Mortgage Industry (With Jobs List)Critical thinkingMortgage brokers often gather information and statistics related to several different lending options and help the borrower make the best decision. They need excellent critical-thinking skills to carefully review each document and all criteria and choose the most viable option for their clients. They may also help their clients determine and find important documents and respond to changing scenarios quickly, which involves critical thinking quickly to ensure all processes occur.Related: 20 Types of Real Estate Jobs (With Salaries and Job Duties)CommunicationThe mortgage process requires requesting employment verifications, pay stubs, credit histories and many other personal details. Being able to communicate those requests and explain the industry and regulatory phrases to borrowers is important for a broker. As they work with a variety of financial employees in the industry, brokers need good communication skills to correspond with all parties.NegotiationThe primary role of a broker is to create a lender-borrower relationship that may last for many years. Brokers act as a liaison between the two parties, and the ability to ensure they agree to common terms employs the use of good negotiation skills. These skills are also important for finding commonalities between the two groups, especially so each one feels content with their decisions to lend and borrow money respectively.Mortgage broker work environmentMortgage brokers work in a fast-paced environment where communication is constant. Some brokers work in an office space with fellow brokers, assistants and other mortgage employees, while others work by themselves in a remote location. Each broker may have a unique working environment, but here are some conditions they usually share:Meeting with clients in an office spaceCommunicating with lenders via phone or emailGenerating new leads by networking with real estate agents, lenders, prospective home buyers and insurance brokersOrganizing multiple mortgages and clients at once, with heavy reliance on computers and telephones to communicateAnswering questions clearly and following up during the various phases of document requirementsReviewing details of legal documents to be able to convey their meaning clearly Repeating similar tasksWorking occasional irregular hours, such as nights and weekends, to meet the needs of borrowersRelated: Trader vs. Broker: What's the Difference?Average salarySalaries for mortgage brokers vary based on their experience, location and brokerage size. Some brokers earn a commission in addition to their salary. According to Indeed Salaries, the national average salary for mortgage brokers in the U.S. is $101,721 per year.For the most up-to-date salary information from Indeed, click on the link(s) provided.Read more: How Much Do Mortgage Brokers Make? (With Duties and FAQs)How to become a mortgage brokerYou can follow these basic steps to become a mortgage broker:1. Complete your educationThe minimum educational requirement to become a mortgage broker is a high school diploma or its equivalent. Some companies prefer a candidate with an associate or bachelor's degree in business administration, accounting or finance. You can choose to earn a college degree to gain more knowledge of financial and analytical topics. It can be helpful to review local mortgage broker job descriptions to determine the best educational path.2. Obtain a broker's licenseFind an accredited institution that provides the 20-hour course required to prepare you for the licensing exam. Visit the NMLS website to find a course that satisfies the requirement in your area. The NMLS exam consists of 125 questions and lasts about four hours. You take the exam at an approved testing center.3. Meet continuing education requirementsThroughout your career, you often have requirements to take continuing education classes as recommended by the NMLS to keep your license current. When you renew your license annually, you submit proof of your continuing education. This ensures you continue to learn and master the skills you need for success as a mortgage broker.4. Find employment as a mortgage brokerSome mortgage brokers work with established companies that assist in building client relationships quickly. Other brokers work independently or on a contract basis. If you want to work with other brokers in an office setting that offers administrative support, search for jobs in brokerage firms. You can also search for contract positions to gain traction in the field and eventually become a self-employed broker. 5. Gain experienceThere are many opportunities for advancement as a broker as you gain experience. Consider finding a mentor that can help you create a defined career path as a broker and make professional industry connections. You can also develop different skills as a mortgage broker depending on the goals and mission of the firm you choose. For example, you may learn more about residential mortgages if you work with a residential firm or more about commercial real estate mortgages if you work with a commercial firm.Read more: How To Become a Mortgage Broker: 7 StepsMortgage broker job description exampleBelow is an example of a mortgage broker job description:We are seeking a vibrant, motivated, organized and experienced mortgage broker to join our brokerage firm. The ideal candidate has a high school diploma, maintains a current license and demonstrates proficiency in all aspects of mortgage origination and closing. They also have at least three years of experience in the field and show good sales and networking techniques.Primary responsibilities include:Acting as the intermediary between potential lenders and borrowersAnalyzing and comparing multiple loans for recommendation to the clientCollecting and assembling required verifications to prepare for closingEnsuring strict compliance with all state and federal regulationsActing as the primary contact for borrower's questions and clarificationsSubmitting relevant documents on timeIf you're interested in a role in real estate, consider one of the following careers related to a mortgage broker: The information on this site is provided as a courtesy and for informational purposes only.
